sections.notes: Always fixed/sticky across the full page. Use support/value messaging only; keep it narrow and persistent.

Use hero content exactly as provided. Left side: headline, subheadline, supporting line, primary and secondary CTAs. Right side: product-related visual if available; if no visual asset, use a brand-safe illustration/abstract product panel. Keep light theme and brand-consistent styling.

Dominant trust signal must be logos. Include Award badge, social proof text 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally', and customer count. Use horizontal flex row with dividers and compact badge treatment on a light grey background.

Show feature support content beneath the headline in a simple readable list/card pattern. Do not invent missing feature items beyond the input.

heroStrategy.headline: Deliver Exceptional Customer Support with Zoho Desk

blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk Customer Support Software | Streamline Ticket Management
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Desk, customer support software for omnichannel ticket management, AI-assisted workflows, and faster customer service across every channel.

sections.backgroundTreatment: soft brand-tinted gradient with a product dashboard collage on the right and minimal decorative support-channel chips
sections.designNote: Keep the hero content-first but dynamic: headline answers what it is, subheadline answers who it is for, CTA answers what to do next. Add a compact value line beneath the CTA and a right-side collage showing inbox, tickets, and AI assistance. Use a small logo lockup and customer count to reinforce continuity with the ad message. Primary CTA button must read 'Get started' and be solid accent orange at 100% opacity.

Immediately follow the hero with a static 3-6 logo grid to satisfy warm-traffic trust strategy. Use recognisable customer logos if available; otherwise, supplement with a compact metric strip and the existing 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' proof line. Keep it restrained, enterprise-clean, and visually quieter than the hero so the page can pivot into explanation.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: How Zoho Desk Works in Under 60 Seconds

sections.designNote: Insert a distinct 3-step process section here, since warm traffic expects quick orientation after trust. Use a left-side numbered step stack and a right-side product UI preview that updates per step: capture, route, resolve. Keep copy concise and scannable, under 60 seconds in reading time. This section should feel process-oriented rather than promotional.

Use proof-led content here rather than another generic feature list. Lead with one strong industry-relevant testimonial spotlight and a supporting row of 2-3 short quotes or outcome statements. Because logos already handled early trust, this section should deepen credibility through outcome language: faster response times, improved visibility, reduced manual work, and better customer satisfaction. Keep the visual treatment more editorial and less structured than the process section.

Merge the multiple product sections into two alternating blocks rather than a generic SaaS feature dump. First block: spotlight-plus-grid for 'Why Choose Zoho Desk?' focusing on omnichannel support, ticket management, AI assistance, and workflow automation. Second block: a visual-forward split panel for Zia AI, with a preview panel on one side and compact feature stack on the other. Since 5+ features exist, avoid a flat static grid; use accordion or spotlight-plus-grid behavior to preserve clarity. Alternate backgrounds and media alignment to avoid repetition.

Treat integrations as a separate utility-focused section with a cleaner, more technical rhythm than the AI block. Present it as a split panel with category chips or a concise app matrix: CRM, collaboration, telephony, e-commerce, automation. This section should feel denser and more practical, with reduced narrative and stronger scanability. Keep it visually distinct from the preceding section by using a white background and simpler surfaces.

Use this as the final feature deep-dive, emphasizing layouts, blueprints, extensions, and help center customization. Make it more flexible and workflow-oriented than the earlier AI and integrations sections. Use a visual-first split panel with a UI mockup or workflow canvas on one side and concise feature text on the other. This section should feel like a capability unlock, not a checklist.

Present pricing as a single highlighted enterprise-style card rather than a comparison table, since the input has one plan. Keep it clean, highly legible, and confidence-building, with included features listed as a vertical checklist. The CTA must remain 'Get started' in solid orange. Keep it visually calmer than the previous section to make the CTA feel like a natural decision point.

Use a 3-card testimonial grid because there are 5 testimonials, and the page needs social proof at the end without turning into a slider-first layout. Mix quote lengths for rhythm and contrast. Prefer support-lead, operations, and founder viewpoints to show broad credibility. Keep the cards restrained with soft shadows, subtle borders, and easy-to-scan author blocks.

Finish with a strong conversion block using a centered floating card or banner-style panel. Since CTA aggression is moderate-to-strong and the traffic is warm, this final section should clearly invite action without overloading the visitor. Use one primary button only: 'Get started'. Make the button full-width on mobile, solid accent orange, and visually dominant. Include a short reassurance line near the CTA rather than a second button.

blueprint.designPersonality: Calm, structured, and enterprise-trustworthy with a light modern SaaS feel. The page should feel efficient and credible, with orange accents used sparingly for action and emphasis, strong logo-led proof, and airy product storytelling similar to the reference but distinctly Techjockey-branded.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use clean SaaS dashboard visuals, support inbox mockups, omnichannel ticket cards, and contextual AI overlays. Keep visuals bright, white-based, and product-led rather than illustrative. Trust proof should be the dominant hero companion: static logo grid, customer-count bar, and compact award chips.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Convert warm visitors into trial or demo starts by proving Zoho Desk is a trustworthy, efficient, omnichannel support platform.
blueprint.narrativeMode: ad-continuity to process clarity to proof to capability depth to conversion

referenceMap.heroPattern: Top-loaded split hero with brand logo lockup, large centered headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet-value line beneath. Primary visual emphasis sits on typography rather than imagery, with the hero content occupying a wide full-width band and minimal distraction.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with stacked content blocks. Initial hero is followed by a lead form panel, then feature sections that read as successive folds. Content density increases after the hero, using repeating section headers and grouped feature lists to maintain scanability.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily plain content blocks rather than highly decorated cards. When card treatment appears, it is functional and form-led, with restrained borders, subtle elevation, and utility-first layout. No strong glass, shadow-heavy, or image-led card language is evident.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA in the hero, reinforced by a nearby secondary CTA. Later sections appear mostly informational with minimal repeated CTA pressure. CTAs are likely button-based and high-contrast, with conversion emphasis concentrated above the fold.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern detected in the provided reference HTML.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference HTML; footer behavior cannot be inferred confidently.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-led header treatment with limited visible media in the captured HTML. The layout favors text and form interaction over hero illustration or product screenshots. Any media presence is likely supplementary rather than central.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeated modular feature sections with bold section headline, supporting description, and a grid/list of feature items. The pattern supports progressive disclosure: broad value proposition first, then grouped capabilities, then integrations or customization details. Sections are labeled by fold/order and presented as a linear reading experience.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-generation form placed directly after the hero, using a card container and stacked fields. Form behavior is conversion-oriented, with multiple hidden inputs for tracking and qualification. This suggests a short visible form with heavier data capture behind the scenes.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Lightweight motion only, primarily carousel-based if enabled. No evidence of elaborate animation systems, parallax, or reveal choreography in the provided HTML.

designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Desk is a solution-aware, single-product lead-gen page where visitors are evaluating support software for operational efficiency. The strongest conversion route is a product-led narrative supported by logos-first trust, since the instruction explicitly says visitors trust logos most. The page should feel light, clean, and brand-consistent with a centered or split hero that prioritizes the message and conversion clarity over imagery. Because the content volume is long, the layout should be balanced and highly scannable, with clear section separation and simple feature presentation rather than nested grids. CTA pressure should be present but not overwhelming: one primary action in the hero, repeated at key decision points, with a sticky top strip to maintain conversion access throughout the page.
